description: Figure 3 presents a bar chart illustrating statistics for a dataset, differentiating between “Open” and “Constrained” sets. The horizontal axis displays the category labels: “Avg. Length,” “Avg. Novelty,” “Vocab. Diversity,” and “LLM-based Features,” listed in that order. The vertical axis, labeled “# Instances,” represents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 100, with tick marks at 10-unit intervals.  For each category, there are two bars presented side-by-side: a blue bar representing “Open” sets and an orange bar representing “Constrained” sets. The “Avg. Length” category shows an “Open” bar reaching approximately 60 and a “Constrained” bar reaching approximately 80.  “Avg. Novelty” shows an “Open” bar at approximately 40 and a “Constrained” bar at approximately 60.  “Vocab. Diversity” shows an “Open” bar at approximately 70 and a “Constrained” bar at approximately 30. Finally, “LLM-based Features” shows an “Open” bar at approximately 20 and a “Constrained” bar at approximately 80. The bars are arranged in groups, with each group representing a specific dataset statistic and comparing the “Open” and “Constrained” sets. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
